name: LMC6482AIMX_NOPB
title: LMC6482 / LMC6484 CMOS rail-to-rail input and output op amps
summary: Dual (LMC6482) and quad (LMC6484) CMOS operational amplifiers whose input common-mode range extends past both supply rails and whose output swings to within millivolts of them. Input current is typically 20 fA, CMRR and PSRR 82 dB, gain bandwidth 1.5 MHz and supply current 0.5 mA per amplifier. They run from 3 V to 15.5 V and come in SOIC, VSSOP and PDIP packages in AI and I grades.

circuits.title: Unity-gain difference amplifier
circuits.description: One amplifier with a RES11A10-Q1 matched pair of 1 kΩ / 1 kΩ dividers forms a gain-of-one difference stage: IN+ is halved onto the noninverting input against REF, IN- feeds the inverting input with the output returned through the other divider, so OUT = (IN+) - (IN-) + REF. C1 and C2 (values not given) filter the two input nodes.
notes: Supply pins are not drawn.

circuits.title: Input current limiting resistor on a 3 V follower
circuits.description: A unity-gain follower on a 3 V supply with a 10 kΩ resistor in series with the noninverting input. The resistor holds the input pin current under the ±5 mA rating when the signal goes far past the rails, for example a ±7.5 V input.

circuits.title: Buffering the ADC12038
circuits.description: Both amplifiers run from the converter's 5 V supply. An LM185Bx reference set by 200 kΩ / 130 kΩ gives 2.048 V for VREF+, fed from 5 V through 12.1 kΩ, 2 kΩ and a 50 Ω trim. The 12.1 kΩ / 2 kΩ junction sits near 2.5 V; amplifier B buffers it through 1 kΩ to drive COM, and amplifier A buffers the AC-coupled input (1 nF) riding on that bias, through 1 kΩ, into the converter input. 500 kΩ ties the bias node to the COM output.

circuits.title: Low-power three-op-amp instrumentation amplifier
circuits.description: Two noninverting input stages with 50 kΩ (0.1%) feedback around RG plus a trim rheostat R1 set the differential gain; a difference stage of four 50 kΩ (0.1%) resistors gives a single-ended output referred to VREF. 10 kΩ resistors Ri limit input current. The 48.7 kΩ and 10 Ω rheostat trim DC common-mode rejection, C4 (3 pF to 20 pF) trims AC common-mode rejection, and C1 (10 pF) balances it.

circuits.description: The two-amplifier structure with a RES11A90-Q1 matched 1 kΩ / 9 kΩ divider pair, giving 10 V/V referred to REF.
notes: Supply pins are not drawn.

circuits.title: 3 V single-supply buffer
circuits.description: A unity-gain follower on a single 3 V supply with a 0.1 µF bypass capacitor from V+ to ground. The input should stay between the rails.

circuits.title: Resistive isolation of a 330 pF load
circuits.description: A follower drives a 330 pF load through 300 Ω placed outside the feedback loop, which keeps the load capacitance from eroding the loop's phase margin. V+ is bypassed with 0.1 µF.

circuits.title: Noninverting stage compensated for a 330 pF load
circuits.description: The output reaches the 330 pF load through R1 = 300 Ω; DC feedback is taken from the load side through 10 kΩ, while C1 = 100 pF from the amplifier output to the inverting input carries the high-frequency feedback and keeps phase margin. R1 and C1 were chosen by experiment for the pulse response.

circuits.title: Feedback capacitor cancelling input capacitance
circuits.description: An inverting stage with R1 in, R2 in feedback and the source or board capacitance CIN at the inverting node. Cf across R2 restores phase margin; start from R1·CIN ≤ R2·Cf and check on the built board.
notes: Supply pins are not drawn.

circuits.title: Offset adjustment, inverting stage
circuits.description: An inverting stage (R1, R2) on ±5 V. A 1 kΩ potentiometer between two 500 kΩ resistors across V+ and V- feeds 1 MΩ into the noninverting input, which has 499 Ω to V-; this gives about ±2.5 mV of input-referred offset adjustment.

circuits.title: Offset adjustment, noninverting stage
circuits.description: A noninverting stage on ±5 V with gain set by R4 against R3. A 500 kΩ potentiometer across V+ and V- injects a small current through R1 into the R2 node, giving about ±2.5 mV of input-referred offset adjustment.

circuits.title: Half-wave rectifier with input current protection
circuits.description: On a single 3 V supply the follower passes the positive half of a ground-centred sine and its output stops at the negative rail for the negative half. Ri = 10 kΩ limits the input pin current when the input goes outside the supply; 10 kΩ closes the loop.

circuits.title: Full-wave rectifier with input current protection
circuits.description: An inverting stage, 10 kΩ in and 10 kΩ feedback taken after a 1N914 diode, on a single supply. Negative inputs are inverted to positive through the diode; for positive inputs the output stage rests at ground and the input passes to VOUT through the two 10 kΩ resistors, so VOUT follows the magnitude of VIN.

circuits.title: Large-compliance-range current source
circuits.description: The amplifier forces the voltage across R (from V+) to equal V+ - VIN by driving a FET's gate, so the transistor delivers IOUT = (V+ - VIN) / R into RL, which goes to ground.

parts.note: pass transistor; pins G gate, S to R, D to RL

circuits.title: Positive supply current sense
circuits.description: Load current IL from V+ flows through R1 = 0.1 Ω. The amplifier drives a FET so that the drop across R2 = 100 Ω equals the drop across R1; the same current returns through the transistor into 1 kΩ, so VOUT = IL × 0.1 Ω × 1 kΩ / 100 Ω, referred to ground.

parts.note: pins G gate, S to R2, D to the 1 kΩ

circuits.title: Low-voltage peak detector with rail-to-rail capture
circuits.description: Amplifier A charges CHOLD = 100 pF through a diode until the hold voltage, buffered by amplifier B, matches the input peak; the 20 kΩ returns the buffered output to A's inverting input and a second diode clamps A's output when the input falls. 1 kΩ isolates the hold node from B's input. A hold capacitor of polyethylene or polystyrene keeps dielectric absorption and leakage low; droop is set by CHOLD and diode leakage.

circuits.title: Rail-to-rail sample-and-hold
circuits.description: Two CD4066B switches driven by VCNTRL connect amplifier A's output to CHOLD and close a local loop around A; amplifier B buffers the hold capacitor through 1 kΩ, and 20 kΩ returns B's output to A's inverting input so the held voltage tracks the input while sampling.

parts.note: one switch of the CD4066B; pins 1, 2 and control C
one switch of the CD4066B; pins 1, 2 and control C

circuits.title: Rail-to-rail single-supply low-pass filter
circuits.description: A two-pole low-pass filter of R1, R2, C1 and C2 with both amplifiers as unity-gain followers; C1 returns the output to the first follower's input. It can serve as an anti-aliasing filter on the converter's supply. With R1 = R2 and C1 = C2 the corner is 1 / (2π R1 C1).

operation.text: CMOS op amps whose input common-mode range and output both reach the supply rails: the LMC6482 is a dual and the LMC6484 a quad. Performance is given for 3 V, 5 V and 15 V supplies and for 2 kΩ and 600 Ω loads; input current is typically 20 fA and CMRR and PSRR 82 dB. They replace TLC272, TLC274, TLC277 and TLC279 parts.

The common-mode range runs 300 mV past either rail. With the common-mode voltage within about 3 V of the positive rail some DC figures, offset voltage in particular, degrade slightly (Figure 6-1). The output stage swings rail to rail even into heavy loads.

An input taken beyond either rail does not invert the output. At room temperature the absolute maximum input is 300 mV past either rail; well beyond that, input current can be large enough to affect reliability, so a series input resistor Ri must hold the pin current to ±5 mA (Figure 6-4: 10 kΩ with a ±7.5 V signal on a 3 V supply).
The output gets to a few hundred mV from each rail. The specified swing figures give an approximate output resistance for sourcing and sinking, which in turn estimates the swing at a given load.
The amplifiers in a package can work independently or be cascaded.

The pinouts are the industry-standard ones. The wider linear input range avoids the nonlinear, slow-recovering output that a narrow-range op amp produces when a signal leaves its common-mode range, which matters in filters where peaking can exceed the range.

Running from the converter's supply, the amplifier needs no input scaling for a limited common-mode range. Its 82 dB CMRR keeps a 12-bit system's integral linearity to ±0.325 LSB, where a rail-to-rail amplifier with only 50 dB CMRR would limit it to about 8 bits.

High input impedance, a wide input range and high common-mode rejection suit instrumentation circuits. In the three-amplifier circuit a small potentiometer in series with RG trims gain more finely and with less vibration sensitivity than one large potentiometer. The discrete version needs 0.01% resistors and two trims for high CMRR and gain accuracy, and discrete resistor drift adds gain error; RES11A matched pairs (matched to better than 0.05%, on one substrate so they drift together) avoid this, e.g. a 1:4 ratio for 36 V/V. The two-amplifier circuit is cheaper and lower power (100 V/V discrete, 10 V/V with RES11A); the three-amplifier circuit suits higher frequencies and wider common-mode range.

A capacitive load forms a pole with the open-loop output impedance (Figure 7-7) and can cause instability, so weigh the output impedance against the closed-loop bandwidth. At unity gain with VS = 15 V the part typically drives 100 pF directly without oscillating; a unity-gain follower tolerates the least. For larger loads, isolate with a series resistor (300 Ω for 330 pF), useful for multiplexer and ADC inputs, or drive the load indirectly with R1 and C1 feeding back high-frequency output to the inverting input (Figure 7-10).

Large feedback resistors are common with this ultra-low input current part; they react with input capacitance from transducers, photodiodes and board parasitics to cut phase margin. A feedback capacitor estimated from R1·CIN ≤ R2·Cf compensates, then check the value on the actual board since board stray capacitance differs from a breadboard's.
The two offset circuits use large resistors and potentiometers to save power and give typically ±2.5 mV of input-referred adjustment with VS = ±5 V.
Ultra-low input current gives negligible offset error with large resistors, which allows smaller, cheaper capacitors.
Operates from 3 V to 15.5 V. Use bypass capacitors from the supply pins to ground and good PCB layout of supply traces and planes for noise immunity.

Circuits needing under 1000 pA of leakage need special PCB layout; to keep the typical 20 fA input current, surface leakage matters, especially with humidity, dust or contamination. Surround the inputs, and every component lead tied to them, with a guard ring on both board sides, driven to the input voltage. Example: 10^12 Ω between a 5 V trace and an input pad leaks 5 pA, 250 times the part's own input current; a guard within 5 mV of the input leaks only 0.05 pA through 10^11 Ω. Guard connections: in an inverting stage the ring goes to the grounded noninverting input; in a noninverting stage and a follower it goes to the inverting-input node (Figures 7-27 to 7-29). Where a PCB is not practical, lift the input pins off the board and solder them directly to the components in air (Figure 7-30).
A SPICE macromodel covers input common-mode range, frequency and transient response, GBW versus load, quiescent and dynamic supply current, and output swing versus load.
